_comment: Every series the metrics endpoint publishes.
This file is the decision, not a record of one. A metric added to the
code without a line here fails the contract test, which is the point: an
operational endpoint grows by one series at a time, each obviously fine
on its own, and nobody re-reads the whole list to notice that it now says
how many people work here and what their projects are called.
Two rules hold for anything added. The value is an aggregate, never a
row: a count of scans is fine, a scan id is not. And the labels are a
closed vocabulary the code owns, never a name that came from a user, so
no project, person, package or repository can appear in the output.
Order is asserted so the emitted document is stable and a diff of two
scrapes reads as a change in values rather than a reshuffle.

series.name: trusca_projects_total
series.help: Projects that exist, archived ones included.

series.name: trusca_scans_total
series.help: Scans by status. The queued and running counts are the ones an operator watches.

series.name: trusca_vulnerability_findings_open
series.help: Open vulnerability findings by severity, across every project.

series.name: trusca_users_active
series.help: Accounts that can sign in. Service accounts are counted separately.

series.name: trusca_service_accounts_active
series.help: Automation identities that can still authenticate.

series.name: trusca_workspace_disk_used_ratio
series.help: Workspace volume in use, 0 to 1. The scan guard refuses above its own threshold.
